pass_a_gloss: Signal with a trumpet upon the earth. The word, the lofty one, the one awakening the hearer, the one preparing him against the passions, the one preparing him against the activities of the opposing things, the one preparing him for the heavenly festivals—for both these things are said—is taken as a trumpet. In Numbers, such a word is a trumpet; for example, the word commands me, and if it is given to another who wishes and seeks the mind of the writings, it commands to make 'silver trumpets, hammered.' Thus the word says: 'Signal with a trumpet upon the earth, and cry aloud, say: Gather together and let us enter into the walled cities.' The word of God does not want us to enter into an unwalled city, but into the church of the living [one] fortified by the word—for this word is the wall. It lies in the seventeenth Psalm, that God also is a fortress. 'Having taken up, flee to Zion': all who are outside Zion, 'having taken up, flee to Zion; hasten, do not stand,' those in the progress hasten to the Watchtower, 'for I bring evil from the north and a great breaking.' Of the evils brought 'from the north,' the north of the opposing thing, as often said, whoever is found not hastening nor having entered 'into the walled cities,' not having become in the churches of God, but standing outside, himself will be seized by the enemies and destroyed. Who then is the enemy? Let us see from the following how it is said: 'A lion rose up from his den, destroying nations, he swept away.' This is the enemy whom we must flee. The lion pursues us. Who is this? Peter Peter teaches saying: 'Your adversary the devil, as a lion roaming about, seeks whom he may devour; whom you resist firm in the faith.' And according to the ninth Psalm: 'He lies in wait in secret, he lies in wait as a lion in his den. And this lion lies in wait not by day, but when it becomes night.' For according to the one hundred and thirtieth Psalm: 'You brought forth darkness and it became night. In it all the beasts of the forest will pass through, cubs roaring to seize and to seek food from God for themselves.'

pass_b_english: 'Signal with a trumpet upon the earth.' (Numbers 10:2–3) The lofty word—the one that wakes the hearer, that prepares him for the fight against the passions and against the activities of opposing powers, that prepares him for the heavenly festivals (for it is said with a view to both)—is taken as a trumpet.

In Numbers such a word is a trumpet. For example, the word commands me—and anyone else to whom it is given who wills and has sought the mind of the Scriptures—to make 'silver trumpets, hammered work.' So the word says: 'Signal with a trumpet upon the earth, and cry aloud; say: Gather yourselves and let us enter the walled cities.' (Jeremiah 4:7) The word of God does not want us to enter an unwalled city, but into the church of the living God, walled by the strength of the Word—for he is the wall. In the seventeenth Psalm it also lies that God is a wall. 'Taking it up, flee into Zion.' As many of you as are outside Zion, 'taking it up, flee into Zion; hurry, do not stand still.' (Psalm 9:11 (LXX)) You who are in progress, hurry to the Lookout, 'for I am bringing evils from the north and a great crushing' (Psalm 139:12 (LXX))—evils brought 'from the north'—from the opposing one, the north, as has often been said. Whoever is found not hurrying and not entering 'into the walled cities,' not becoming 'in the churches of God,' but standing outside, will himself be caught by the enemies and destroyed. Who is the enemy? Let us see from what follows how it is said: 'A lion has gone up from his den; destroying nations he has carried them off.' This is the enemy we must flee. A lion pursues us. Who is this? Peter teaches, saying: 'Your adversary the devil walks about like a roaring lion seeking whom he may swallow; resist him, firm in the faith.' And according to the ninth Psalm he 'lies in wait in secret; he lies in wait like a lion in his den.' And this lion does not lie in wait by day, but when night has come. For according to the hundred-and-third Psalm: 'You set darkness, and it became night. In it all the beasts of the wood will pass through, young lions roaring to snatch and to seek from God food for themselves.'
